items.line: A year after Washington ended its EV credit, US makers drop electric pickups while Chinese makers price higher and sell abroad.
items.what: A European, Korean or Japanese maker cuts electric car or device production or jobs and names Chinese competition as a reason.
items.because: The join says Chinese makers grow where others shrink, so the pressure should show outside the US, where Chinese goods are not kept out by tariffs.

items.line: Governments are using pardons and refusals to sign laws, and courts and heads of state are now being asked to overrule them.
items.what: A court in Serbia, Malaysia or Taiwan agrees to hear a challenge to a pardon or to the cabinet's refusal to countersign a law.
items.because: If these single-office acts are moving into the courts, at least one of the disputes should reach a judge within weeks, which a set of separate political rows would not require.

items.line: Governments are using pardons and refusals to sign laws, and courts and heads of state are now being asked to overrule them.
items.what: A government in a seventh country refuses to sign, publish or apply a law passed by its parliament.
items.because: If the shape is a general turn towards using acts one office controls against legislatures, it should appear outside these six countries; unrelated national rows would not predict it.

items.line: El Niño is expected to bring drought, but its first weeks have brought storms and landslides to mountain cities and the Pacific coast.
items.what: Peru declares a state of emergency over rain or flooding in Tumbes, Piura or another northern coastal region.
items.because: If the Tumbes rain is the start of a coastal El Niño rather than a single storm, it will continue for weeks and reach the level of an emergency, which a passing storm would not.

items.line: El Niño is expected to bring drought, but its first weeks have brought storms and landslides to mountain cities and the Pacific coast.
items.what: Peru's ENFEN or Colombia's IDEAM links the current rains to El Niño or raises its El Niño alert level.
items.because: If the rains share the cause the Bogotá report names, the agencies that forecast El Niño will say so; if they are ordinary seasonal storms, they will not.

items.line: With the US-Iran war paused, Washington presses Iran by land and sea while Saudi Arabia and the Houthis trade strikes.
items.what: Iraq's government announces that it has closed one or more of its border crossings with Iran.
items.because: If the pause is a change of method rather than an end, Washington's request should become an Iraqi act rather than stay a reported conversation.

items.line: With the US-Iran war paused, Washington presses Iran by land and sea while Saudi Arabia and the Houthis trade strikes.
items.what: The US Treasury announces new sanctions on Iranian oil exports, tankers or a named Iranian company.
items.because: Pressure by land and sea without strikes needs a financial part, and the join predicts it arrives while Trump still calls war unlikely.

items.line: Courts now reach presidents and their deputies through their assets and declared wealth, while elsewhere they try the opposition.
items.what: A court in another Latin American country freezes the assets of a current or former president, vice-president or minister.
items.because: If asset freezes have become the usual route to people at the top of government, Paraguay's case should not stand alone for long.

items.line: Courts now reach presidents and their deputies through their assets and declared wealth, while elsewhere they try the opposition.
items.what: Armenian prosecutors bring a corruption, tax or money-laundering charge against an opposition leader or an opposition-linked businessman.
items.because: If whether a case follows money or politics depends on who holds office, the next case against Armenia's opposition should be framed as money.

items.line: Legal routes to work abroad are now so few that they go by lottery, while irregular routes still kill dozens at a time.
items.what: A second labour-sending country uses a lottery or ballot to allocate jobs or work visas abroad.
items.because: If legal routes are rationed rather than merely slow, other sending governments facing more applicants than places should ration the same way.

items.line: Legal routes to work abroad are now so few that they go by lottery, while irregular routes still kill dozens at a time.
items.what: Malaysia or a Gulf state announces a cap, freeze or new quota on workers from Bangladesh.
items.because: A lottery implies a fixed number of places set by the receiving country, and the join predicts those numbers are being cut rather than raised.

items.line: Twenty-five years after joining the WTO, Chinese makers sell abroad at luxury prices as well as low ones.
items.what: A Chinese carmaker announces a new factory or assembly plant outside China.
items.because: If export markets are now where Chinese makers plan their profits, production should follow the sales to get inside the tariffs that face them.

items.line: Twenty-five years after joining the WTO, Chinese makers sell abroad at luxury prices as well as low ones.
items.what: A US, European or Japanese carmaker announces a deal to use a Chinese maker's electric platform, batteries or software.
items.because: A US maker withdrawing an electric model while Chinese makers move up the market predicts that others will license Chinese technology rather than build their own.

items.line: Four years after ChatGPT, so much rests on one chip firm that its chief's private life moves share prices and chip policy.
items.what: A US bill or Commerce Department rule to tighten Chinese access to AI chips is introduced, with the Nvidia spy allegation named as a reason.
items.because: If the affair is treated as a security matter because Nvidia carries the AI build, its first lasting result should be law, not only a share price.

items.line: Four years after ChatGPT, so much rests on one chip firm that its chief's private life moves share prices and chip policy.
items.what: Shares of TSMC, SK Hynix or another Nvidia supplier fall 5% or more in a day, with Nvidia's troubles named as the cause.
items.because: Concentration means a fall at Nvidia should reach the firms whose revenue depends on it, which a stand-alone celebrity scandal would not.

items.line: Oil prices now follow what Trump says about Iran talks more than the attacks on the Saudi pipeline that bypasses Hormuz.
items.what: Brent is reported lower over a week in which a further strike on Saudi or Emirati oil infrastructure is also reported.
items.because: If prices follow statements about talks rather than events around the Gulf, a strike on the bypass routes should not reverse the fall.

items.line: Oil prices now follow what Trump says about Iran talks more than the attacks on the Saudi pipeline that bypasses Hormuz.
items.what: Saudi Arabia or Aramco reports reduced flows, repairs or a halt on the East-West pipeline or at Yanbu after an attack.
items.because: If the fighting has moved to the routes built to avoid Hormuz, the damage should show there rather than in the strait.

items.line: As the last four years are confirmed the hottest, governments seek new gas and LNG while the climate summit plans electrification.
items.what: The COP31 final text is adopted with electrification or grid targets but without a dated commitment to phase out or transition away from fossil fuels.
items.because: If governments are securing gas while the summit plans electrification, the text should set power targets and leave gas untouched.

items.line: As the last four years are confirmed the hottest, governments seek new gas and LNG while the climate summit plans electrification.
items.what: A European or Asian government approves a new domestic gas field, a gas drilling trial or an LNG import contract and cites supply security.
items.because: The join holds only if the turn to gas is policy across importing countries rather than a handful of unrelated projects.
